source.title: Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns
source.authors: Nusret Cakici; Syed Jawad Hussain Shahzad; Barbara Bedowska-Sojka; Adam Zaremba

hypothesis: Coins with higher recent market-adjusted alpha continue to outperform coins with lower recent alpha over the following week.
mechanism: The source identifies past alpha among the most important simple predictors in the crypto cross-section and reports persistent abnormal returns with limited benefit from complex models.
market_factor: Equal-weight hourly log return across contemporaneously available panel assets.
signal: Rolling market-model intercept alpha = mean(asset return) - beta*mean(market return), with beta=cov/var, using returns only through the prior completed hour.
universe: Point-in-time assets with exact hourly history and top 80 percent by lagged trailing 30-day close*volume; minimum 8 assets.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC; execute at current open.
construction: Equal-weight long top-alpha quartile / short bottom-alpha quartile, 0.5 gross per side.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >= 0.02, HAC p < 0.05, positive top-minus-bottom subsequent-week return, at least 100 weekly observations.
limitations: Equal-weight market return substitutes for a point-in-time capitalization-weighted crypto market factor; the prepared panel contains 19 liquid perps and funding is not present.
